summary: 39-year-old woman with a 2.8 cm nodule and suppressed TSH. ATA 2015/2016: subnormal TSH → radionuclide scan; a hyperfunctioning ("hot") nodule does not need FNA; symptomatic beta-blockade; definitive radioiodine or surgery.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Lump in the front of the neck
inputs.hpi: Right-sided neck lump for 4 months. Over the last 2 months: palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor and 4 kg weight loss. No eye symptoms. No voice change or swallowing difficulty.

exam.general: Fine tremor, warm sweaty palms, pulse 104 regular. 3 cm smooth right thyroid nodule, rest of gland impalpable. No eye signs. No lymphadenopathy.

imaging.name: USS thyroid
imaging.result: Right lobe 2.8 cm solid isoechoic nodule with peripheral vascularity, smooth margins (TI-RADS TR3). Left lobe small. No abnormal nodes.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Probable toxic adenoma (right) — suppressed TSH, 2.8 cm nodule
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hyperthyroidism with a solitary 2.8 cm right nodule (TSH suppressed) — probable toxic adenoma. Radionuclide uptake scan before any FNA; beta-blocker for symptoms; definitive treatment with radioiodine or hemithyroidectomy.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = cholecystitis, GORD, PUD: SOCRATES answers carry no thyrotoxic features (heat intolerance/palpitations are chips, not SOCRATES text). PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.

mustInclude.note: ATA 2015: if the serum TSH is subnormal, a radionuclide thyroid scan should be obtained.

mustExclude.note: Hyperfunctioning nodules are rarely malignant and do not need FNA.

guideline.name: 2015 American Thyroid Association guidelines — thyroid nodules and differentiated thyroid cancer
guideline.section: Nodule evaluation (TSH first; radionuclide scan when TSH is subnormal; hyperfunctioning nodules do not need FNA); cytology-directed management; extent of surgery (total thyroidectomy for cN1 disease)
guideline.citation: Haugen BR, Alexander EK, Bible KC, et al. 2015 American Thyroid Association management guidelines for adult patients with thyroid nodules and differentiated thyroid cancer. Thyroid. 2016;26:1–133.

guideline.name: 2016 ATA guidelines — hyperthyroidism and other causes of thyrotoxicosis
guideline.section: Toxic adenoma: radionuclide uptake scan, beta-blockade, definitive treatment (radioactive iodine or surgery)
guideline.citation: Ross DS, Burch HB, Cooper DS, et al. 2016 American Thyroid Association guidelines for diagnosis and management of hyperthyroidism and other causes of thyrotoxicosis. Thyroid. 2016;26:1343–1421.

rationale: Permutation: suppressed TSH. The work-up order changes (scan before cytology). Quality only: the risk is unnecessary FNA and missed hyperthyroidism treatment, not immediate harm.
